title: A struggling AI trade is dragging stocks lower ahead of Anthropic’s mega-IPO
excerpt: AI-linked shares struggled on Monday as investors headed for Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's hotly anticipated IPO.
content_html:
By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-16T18:42:39.353Z

The AI trade was struggling again on Monday as investors headed toward new catalysts with the potential to rewire the bull market.

Tech stocks were shaken on as traders fretted about the health of the AI trade ahead of Anthropic's IPO. The sector was dragged lower chiefly by Nvidia, which dropped another 3% as the Commerce Department moved to close a policy loophole that has allowed firms in China to access advanced Nvidia chips.

Nvidia, whose web of partnerships form the core of the AI trade, has been roiled by scandal in the last week. Investors are struggling to envision the future of the company and the industry without Jensen Huang, who stepped down as CEO last week after a series of scandals related to relationships with Nvidia insiders and a suspected Chinese spy.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on the company to make major changes over the weekend and to bring in a new CEO from outside. President Donald Trump, in contrast, said he supported the idea of Huang one day returning to Nvidia.

Nvidia shares tanked another 2%, pulling down other chipmakers, neoclouds, and data center operators within its orbit.

Comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, meanwhile, may have exacerbated the skittishness in the AI sector. Speaking in San Francisco on Monday, the central bank chief called AI important to the economy but warned that the technology could dissapoint. He outlined a scenario in which stock prices tumble and spark an economic downturn.

The selling accelerated into the afternoon as investors took in Warsh's comments. Major indexes sank into the red, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropping nearly 3%.

Here's where US indexes stood around 1:30 p.m. ET:

  • S&P 500: 7,414.59, down 1.95%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 51,676.27, down 1.28% (-671.28 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 27,160.96, down 2.8%

The latest tech woes come at a tough time for Anthropic, which is gear up for a long-awaited market debut. The Claude parent is chasing a $1.4 trillion valuation, with pricing expected on Wednesday and its trading debut set for Thursday. The event is a make-or-break moment for the tech sector, with investor reception to the IPO critical to the narrative of continued AI bullishness.

Investors are also looking ahead to Nvidia's third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday and new Personal Consumption Expenditures data on Wednesday.

Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO will be major tests for the market, Brian Therien, a senior analyst at Edward Jones, wrote in a note.

"Together, we expect NVIDIA's results and Anthropic's market debut to provide important tests of whether investor enthusiasm for AI continues to be supported by earnings growth and demand for public-market exposure," Therien said.

"The bigger question for the AI trade isn't whether Nvidia or Anthropic delivers, but whether investors are putting new money to work or simply rotating between winners and losers," Mark Hackett, the chief market strategist at Nationwide, said.
